reason: Validation selected a draw threshold of 0.28, which raised 2023/24 macro F1 by +0.027 without changing accuracy. title: Dixon-Coles goal model and compact odds-free feature set
hypothesis: A goal-based model or a smaller feature set improves the independent signal.
statistical_uncertainty: Validation gains were below the pre-registered 0.002 log-loss margin or lost accuracy.
reason: Standalone Dixon-Coles reached 56.8% validation accuracy and was clearly weaker than the production blend. A validation-selected 0.08 blend improved validation log loss by only +0.0003, below the 0.002 gate. No goal-model component is promoted. The 143-feature odds-free core set improved validation log loss by +0.0045 but changed validation accuracy by -2.63%. The accuracy gate was missed, so the full odds-free feature set is retained.

statistical_uncertainty: On the already-examined 760 test matches the production model won 2 matches the market missed and lost 0 (exact McNemar p=1.00). The paired accuracy difference is +0.26% (95% CI +0.00% to +0.66%). Probability quality is slightly worse than the market: log-loss difference -0.0058 (market minus model). reason: Every justified challenger was evaluated on 2023/24 validation and replicated with expanding-window walk-forward origins. None cleared its pre-registered gate, so the existing production ensemble and argmax decision rule are retained. The model matches market accuracy within noise and has marginally worse probability quality; no bookmaker-beating claim is supported.
